segments.text: Good morning everyone. Thanks for being here today.
I want to talk about the problem we noticed after running thirty customer interviews last quarter.
Our users are losing 2.3 hours per week, per person, to context switching between tools. That's not a feeling; that's from our anonymised product analytics panel of 4,800 active seats.
Every product on the market claims to fix workflow. Most of them add another tab. We're doing something different.
Instead of another tool, we're adding a thin layer on top of what you already use. One keyboard shortcut, zero new accounts.
We ran a closed beta with twelve teams for four weeks. The average time saved was exactly the number I led with: 2.3 hours per week per engineer.
If that sounds like something you'd want to try, I'd love to get you into the beta after this.

nextStep.fullBody: Hi Jordan — I have a pitch Tuesday and just ran the coach on my rough take. The main thing it flagged: I rushed the 2.3-hours key stat and it came out more nervous than emphatic. Would you have 10 minutes tomorrow to watch me run it once more? No need to prepare, just listen for whether the key claim lands heavy or light. Thanks — really appreciate it.
